Origami introduces S1 glove for recording finger motion and touch

Twenty finger-joint measurements are synchronized with tactile data and video, using a joint layout matched to the company’s robot hand.

Humanoids Daily ↗21 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Recording what images miss

Origami Robotics introduced S1 on October 21. Encoders measure 20 finger-joint angles alongside fingertip and palm pressure and synchronized video, retaining motion data under occlusion. The musical demonstrations record human skills; they do not establish that a robot can reproduce the performances.

Matching capture to execution

The glove and robot hand share a joint layout, allowing calibrated measurements to become robot joint targets directly. Origami compared fingertip positions against OptiTrack and reports millimeter-level accuracy in that recording, rather than a guarantee across all tasks and wearers.

Production and transfer limitations

The company replaced a rigid factory-trial design with a soft shell to accommodate more hands and says mass production has begun, without a firm price or shipping schedule. Differences between human and robot fingertips still change object contact; a model to address that gap remains in development.
